answers.children: Yes — Clumber Spaniels are good with children thanks to their calm and patient demeanor especially with families and their gentle affectionate nature. Their heavy sturdy build means they tolerate ear-tugging from toddlers without grumbling yet their determined hunting instinct can surface during play so they pull with surprising strength when a scent catches their low-slung frame. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Clumber Spaniels generally get along with other pets because of their gentle temperament and low prey drive as flushing retrievers rather than chasers. Their affectionate side extends to household animals once they warm up though they can remain aloof with strangers or dogs initially due to their aristocratic hunting background.
answers.exercise: Clumber Spaniels need 30 to 60 minutes of moderate exercise daily such as a leisurely walk or slow backyard romp that matches their sturdy low-slung build developed for methodical work in dense underbrush. Without it their strong scenting ability leads them to lounge excessively and they gain weight rapidly given their heavy frame and tendency toward packing on pounds.
answers.shedding: Yes — Clumber Spaniels shed moderately with a medium-length coat that is dense enough to trap hair around the home. Their feathering on legs and tail combined with the heavy spaniel build means loose fur appears year-round especially during seasonal changes and requires regular removal to prevent mats in their thick coat.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Clumber Spaniel is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its medium dense coat with feathering sheds enough to spread dander while the sturdy low-slung body carries loose hair into furniture making it unsuitable for strict allergy management.
answers.training: Clumber Spaniels are moderately easy to train because their intelligence of 7 supports learning yet their stubborn streak and determined nature bred for independent scent work in underbrush can make them resistant to commands. Their calm patient demeanor helps during sessions but owners must counter the tendency to ignore cues when a scent overrides focus.
answers.lifespan: Clumber Spaniels live 10-12 years. Their heavy sturdy build and tendency to gain weight from a low energy level of 5 place extra strain on their frame during daily lounging which can influence longevity alongside their gentle but determined hunting heritage.
answers.size: Clumber Spaniels reach 55-85 lb and stand 17-20 in tall as adults. Their heavy low-slung frame the heaviest among spaniels feels substantial when they choose a lap for lounging and their blocky heads and sturdy proportions reflect the deliberate breeding for steady flushing work rather than speed.
answers.barking: Clumber Spaniels do not bark a lot. Their quiet mellow nature leads to low rumbling woofs only when something is truly amiss rather than at every leaf reflecting their original role as aristocratic hunting companions who worked methodically without unnecessary noise.
answers.apartment: Yes — Clumber Spaniels can live in an apartment because their calm patient demeanor and low energy of 5 allow them to settle indoors as dedicated loungers. Their minimal barking and moderate exercise needs of 30-60 minutes suit smaller spaces as long as their sturdy build does not lead to weight gain from inactivity.
answers.first-time: Clumber Spaniels are not the best choice for first-time owners because their stubborn streak during training and tendency to gain weight demand consistent management that novices may find challenging. Their affectionate gentle side rewards experienced handlers who understand the determined fieldwork roots behind the couch-potato habits.
